Meta New Grad Interview Experience
I just finished my New Grad SWE Interview and I'm not sure how it went.


Valid Palindrome with removing one character - explained brute force and optimal solution and solved it optimally, follow up: asked me Valid Palindrome with removing k characters but just told me to say my approach (not code it) and asked for time complexity

I honeslty thought I failed this interview because of the second question so having my second technical interview right after this wasn't the best.


Range Sum of BST- I solved it brute force (visiting all the nodes in the tree) and then solved it again optimally.
Number of Islands but you have to find the "properties" in the island bordering water. I explained the optimal approach but turns out I didn't fully understand the problem. I wrote the code out and missed one edge case (if the property is at the edge of the graph it counts as a property bordering water). After I wrote my code we walked through a test case but didn't have time to finish as we were almost out of time. Right after the interview ended, I realized my mistake.
Behavioral - I did this round a few weeks ago and don't remember much but it seemed to go well.

Microsoft SWE Intern (Summer 2026) Interview Experience [India] [Virtual]
**Status:** Awaiting Decision
**Position:** Software Engineer Intern
**Location:** India (Virtual Campus Hiring)
**Date:** October 2025
___

## **Process:**
1.  **Online Assessment (OA):** 1 round on HackerRank.
2.  **Technical Interviews:** 2 virtual rounds back-to-back. The final decision is made after Round 2.

---
### **Online Assessment (OA)**

* **Platform:** HackerRank
* **Duration:** 60 Minutes
* **Questions:** 2 coding problems.
* **Difficulty:** The problems were different for everyone, but the general difficulty was 1 LeetCode Easy and 1 LeetCode Medium.

---
### **Technical Round 1 (Approx. 50-60 mins)**

This round was scheduled for 40-45 minutes but ran longer. It was a mix of behavioral and technical DSA questions.

1.  **Introduction & Behavioral:** Started with "Tell me about yourself." This led to a behavioral question: "Tell me about the biggest technical difficulty you faced in one of your projects and how you overcame it."
    * *My advice:* I discussed a backend performance/scalability issue I identified in a personal project and the optimization I implemented to fix it.
2.  **DSA Problem 1 (Graph Traversal):**
    * A LeetCode Medium-style graph traversal problem.
    * I discussed my initial approach using **DFS (Depth-First Search)**, including time and space complexity.
    * The interviewer then **modified the problem constraints** and asked what changes I would make to my code. I discussed the new logic.
    * After I coded the DFS solution, she asked how I would solve it using **BFS (Breadth-First Search)**. I explained the queue-based approach orally.
3.  **DSA Problem 2 (Event Cooldown System):**
    * This was a design/implementation problem. The task was to process a stream of incoming events of different types (e.g., Type 0, Type 1, Type 2).
    * Each event type had its own specific **cooldown period**.
    * The function needed to return `true/false` for an incoming event based on whether its cooldown had passed since the *last successful execution of that same event type*.
    * I solved this by explaining a **Hash Map**-based approach to store the last execution timestamp for each event type and compare it against the current time and the required delay.

---
### **Technical Round 2 (Approx. 30 mins)**

Sharing my recent Microsoft Software Engineer interview experience. The process consisted of 4 rounds, with each round being approximately 45 minutes.

## Background
- Currently Laid off
- 5 YOE, Worked in Product Based MNC (FAANG)

## Round 1 — Coding / Problem Solving

- The first round was a coding round and was eliminatory.


```
The question was to design an Expression Evaluator.
Given a mathematical expression containing:

+, -, *, /
Parentheses
Multi-digit integers
Spaces
Unary + / -

The evaluator had to return the integer result while respecting standard operator precedence.

Example
-7 + 5 * 8 - 5 / 4 + (5 + 4)

The main focus was on:

Parsing the expression
Operator precedence
Handling nested parentheses
Handling unary operators
Multi-digit numbers
Edge cases

This round was eliminatory, so getting to a correct approach was important.
```

The second round was an LLD round.

Problem: Design a Library Management System

The discussion covered:

Identifying the core entities
Defining classes and their responsibilities
Relationships between entities
Borrowing and returning books
Handling different types of users/books
Extensibility of the design
Implementation-level decisions

The interviewer went beyond just drawing a class diagram and discussed how the system would actually be implemented.

Product search, filtering and sorting

10M products

Resume walkthrough

Follow-up questions based on my experience

DSA Round | Walmart | SWE - III (IN3) | 4 YoE | Rejected
Hi all,

I was reached by a recruiter from Walmart 6 days ago that my profile has been shortlisted for the SWE-III profile and they will schedule the interview for 16th July.

I tried to follow up about the time slot almost daily, and guess what yesterday at 10pm they said they had some misunderstanding and they would schedule for 16th July at 11am.

Point 1 : Why did they assign the slot this late ? Honestly I was a bit dicey if I will be called for an interview or not. And hence, lost interest for prep (which I already started and continued for 2-3 days).


Questions asked :
Question 1 :
Difference between String, stringBuilder & stringBuilder
As a follow-up one output question was about the same. (I was able to do it in a minute or so)

Question 2 :
I was given two classes as follows
```
class Employee{
    private String name;
    private int id;
    private Age age;
}
class Age{
    int day;
    int month;
    int year;
}
```
The task was to make the class Employee as an immutable class.
I was able to solve it within the time.

Question 3:
Basic Calculator - III
I was able to explain my thought process and started coding.
But my code became a bit messy, although I was using Stack, but found the question quite lengthy.
Hence, was not able to solve it completely.

I have some doubts :
